recentItems.title: Innovation is Never Finished | Camilo Fero | TEDxClevelandStateUniversity
recentItems.description:
What happens when an invention’s greatest strength becomes its lasting problem? Drawing on his work in sustainability and plastic chemistry, Camilo Ferro explores how we can preserve the benefits of our inventions while addressing their unintended consequences. From detergents and refrigerants to today’s plastics, he asks whether we can change an invention’s ending by changing its beginning and why our responsibility to improve it never ends. Camilo A. Ferro is an entrepreneur and sustainability innovator with more than 15 years of experience developing solutions to plastic waste. He founded Earth 2 Earth, served as vice president of sustainability and innovation at Nature's Source and is president of RAWS Americas. 

In that role, he is helping bring to market a plastics technology designed to eliminate persistent plastic waste without creating microplastics. Throughout his career, Ferro has focused on advancing sustainability through innovation grounded in scientific research, transparency and practical implementation, with the goal of creating solutions that are both environmentally responsible and commercially viable. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

What if the biggest barriers to progress are not the challenges we face, but the way we perceive them? In this thought-provoking talk, Santanu Basu invites audiences to question conventional thinking, challenge established perspectives, and explore new possibilities. By examining how curiosity, critical thinking, and a willingness to embrace change can reshape our understanding of the world, he encourages people to move beyond familiar assumptions and discover fresh approaches to everyday challenges. The talk inspires audiences to rethink what they believe, see opportunities where others see limitations, and turn new perspectives into meaningful action. Santanu Basu is the Founder of Let’s Game Now and a pioneering figure in India’s esports ecosystem. A former professional FIFA esports player, he represented India internationally and competed in 50+ tournaments. With over 15 years of gaming experience, he has contributed significantly to India’s competitive gaming landscape through esports tournaments, communities and initiatives aimed at creating sustainable opportunities for the next generation of gamers. recentItems.description:

What if the music in our playlist could do more than entertain us?

In this thought-provoking TEDx talk, Gauri Yadwadkar explores the therapeutic potential of Indian Raag music and its connection with the human mind and body. Drawing from the ancient traditions of Indian classical music and emerging neuroscience research, she examines how specific raags may influence attention, emotional regulation, stress, and overall wellbeing.

From Raga Darbari and Jogiya to the ancient sound of Aum, the talk brings together tradition and modern science to ask a simple question: What if, instead of asking what music we like, we asked what music our brain needs today?

The talk offers a perspective on music not as a replacement for medicine, but as a potential companion to healthcare, self-care, and emotional wellbeing. Perhaps the most powerful medicine we carry every day isn’t in our pocket. It’s in our playlist. Head of Content / A&R (Non-Film) at Times Music, the label under Bennett, Coleman & Co.(Times Group), with over two decades on the music scene. She focuses on non-film repertoire, Indian classical, devotional, folk and independent music, with releases like 'Maula' featuring Gulzar (2018) and 'Saanwal', produced by Ustad Zakir Hussain. Drawing on her experience as a physical therapist, Dr. Kathleen Stross introduces Hineni, an ancient Hebrew word meaning “Here I am,” and reimagines it as a practical framework for facing fear, overcoming avoidance, and expanding our lives through action. Rather than waiting to feel ready, she argues that meaningful change begins when awareness becomes movement. Through powerful stories, neuroscience, and a simple three-step practice, this talk shows how one embodied step can transform the way we meet life's challenges. Kathleen Stross is a Doctor of Physical Therapy and holistic health practitioner who has spent over three decades helping people reclaim their balance—physically, emotionally, and personally. A pioneer in vestibular rehabilitation, she is known for her ability to translate science into hope and practical action. Through her work at In Harmony, Kathleen empowers individuals to separate who they are from what they’ve been diagnosed with, rebuilding identity and possibility with compassion and clarity. recentItems.title: A Blueprint for the Next Generation | Major Hemendra K. Singh | TEDxCUH
recentItems.description:
NOTE FROM TED: This talk only represents the speaker’s personal views. We've flagged this talk because it falls outside the content guidelines TED gives TEDx organizers.  TEDx events are independently organized by volunteers. The guidelines we give TEDx organizers are described in more detail here: http://storage.ted.com/tedx/manuals/tedx_content_guidelines.pdf

What if the ultimate blueprint for a nation's future could be found in the selfless courage of twenty-something soldiers from its past?   

Drawing inspiration from the staggering heights of the Kargil war memorials, this talk contrasts the mission-driven leadership of young military personnel with the individualistic, career-focused anxieties of modern youth. The presentation challenges the audience to envision the year 2047, asking whether they want to simply inherit a better country, or be the ones who actively build it.   

To achieve this vision, the talk outlines a powerful five-point framework for the next generation: choose a larger purpose over a mere position, act with courage in the face of fear, and embrace a continuous cycle of learning, unlearning, and relearning in a rapidly shifting job market. Furthermore, it emphasizes the need to prioritize authentic character over curated social media profiles, and to value active contribution over passive consumption. Ultimately, this presentation serves as a rallying cry to shift from being mere passengers on the journey of progress to becoming its core architects. Maj Hemendra K. Singh (Retd.) represents a rare convergence of battlefield leadership, institutional business strategy, and technology-led governance transformation. Commissioned into the Indian Army in 2001, he served in high-risk counter-insurgency operations in Jammu & Kashmir, where leadership demanded resilience under uncertainty, disciplined execution, and strategic clarity. 
Transitioning into corporate leadership, he currently serves as Corporate Vice President & National Head – Defence Affinity Business at Axis Max Life Insurance, leading one of India’s most specialised institutional verticals. His mandate spans strategic partnerships across the Armed Forces ecosystem, scalable institutional growth models, financial inclusion, AI-enabled transformation, and ESG-aligned value creation within regulated financial markets. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Can We Rebuild the Brain? | Sean Simonini | TEDxBoston Salon
recentItems.description:
NOTE FROM TED: Research discussed in this talk remains an ongoing field of study. TEDx events are independently organized by volunteers. The guidelines we give TEDx organizers are described in more detail here: http://storage.ted.com/tedx/manuals/tedx_content_guidelines.pdf

When neurons die, our brains have little capacity to make new ones. This has meant that neurodegenerative conditions, traumatic brain injuries, strokes, and age-related decline have all been considered permanent and irreversible. 

Sean Simonini learned this the hard way, but sees hope in our ability to reverse this damage by transplanting new neurons into the brain. 

He traces how cell replacement therapies, from early trials in Parkinson’s to cutting edge science, are beginning to break the long-held belief that damage to the brain could never be undone. He argues that neurology is shifting from preserving what is left, to restoring what was lost, and asks what this means when new cells become a part of us.  Sean Simonini is a Co-Founder & CEO of Sequel Neuroscience which is working on regenerative therapies for stroke, ALS, and other brain conditions. Previously, he was a researcher at the University of California, San Francisco and Harvard University, studying stem cell biology and neurodevelopment. He also led several nonprofits to grow the Boston biotech ecosystem, support public education, and address food insecurity. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What I learned when the worst happened, as a parent | Lindsey Wahlstrom | TEDxMtHood
recentItems.description:
In this deeply personal talk, Lindsey Wahlstrom shares the lessons she learned as both a clinical research professional and a mother navigating her daughter Rona’s rare disease treatment. And how she is finding hope and purpose after her daughter's death.  

Lindsey Wahlstrom works at the intersection of medical research, caregiving, and meaning-making. After more than a decade supporting patient engagement across 200+ clinical trials, Lindsey’s understanding of success in healthcare was radically reshaped when her daughter, Rona, was diagnosed with and died from a rare disease in 2023. She is the co-founder and Chief Momatologist of Rona’s FUN LAB, a nonprofit supporting critically ill children and the teams who care for them, alongside her ongoing work in patient engagement and research. Her work challenges how we define outcomes — and what it truly means to help.

recentItems.title: What disappearing birds are trying to tell us | Pippin Frisbie-Calder | TEDxBatonRouge
recentItems.description:
Nearly three billion birds have disappeared from North America in the past fifty years. The data is overwhelming, and somehow it isn't moving us fast enough. Pippin Frisbie-Calder has spent her career asking why we struggle to act on what we already know, and what art can do about it. Working at the intersection of printmaking, ecological science, and advocacy, she uses large-scale installations and collaborations with researchers to transform statistics about species loss into experiences people can feel. Her talk opens with a sound that no longer exists, the call of the extinct Ivory-billed Woodpecker, and builds a case for art as one of the most underused tools in the climate response.

Pippin Frisbie-Calder is a visual artist and environmental printmaker based in Louisiana whose large-scale woodcuts, silkscreen prints, and immersive installations bring the threatened ecosystems of the Gulf South into galleries, classrooms, and public spaces. She collaborates closely with scientists and conservation organizations, including the Audubon Society, to translate research into art that is both visually compelling and urgently relevant. Her artist residencies have included the Louisiana State University Veterinary Teaching Hospital and A Studio in the Woods in New Orleans. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: How to repair a relationship in 3 steps | Pearl Moses | TEDxArden University Manchester
recentItems.description:
Everyone makes mistakes—but the heartbeat of who we are is revealed in the seconds after. This talk invites us to trade defensiveness for courage: name the misstep, own the impact, and take action to repair. Accountability isn’t a public confession; it’s a practical promise that restores dignity and rebuilds trust. When leaders model honest responsibility, individuals and teams feel safe to speak up, learn faster, and grow stronger together. Repair over perfection creates cultures where people can be imperfect and still be dependable. Choose repair—and you don’t just recover from failure; you reshape what’s possible. 

Pearl Moses is Compliance Director at Setfords Law Ltd and a solicitor with several years’ experience in regulatory compliance, legal publishing, and private practice. Formerly Risk and Compliance Lead at the Law Society of England and Wales, she has held senior regulatory roles and serves on the Law Society’s Legal Compliance Bulletin’s editorial board. Pearl is a sought after speaker and is author of Owning Up to Mistakes, an ethics  and culture focused book published by the Law Society of England and Wales. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
